title: How to Cook a Turkey Breast
excerpt: There is something wonderfully comforting about a golden turkey breast filling the kitchen with the savory aroma of herbs and roasted garlic. This simple recipe brings that cozy holiday feeling to an ordinary family dinner, with tender slices, crisp skin, and plenty of pan juices for spooning over every bite.

Why This Turkey Breast Works

  • It brings the comfort of a holiday meal to an ordinary family dinner.
  • Herb butter seasons the skin, while a thermometer helps you avoid overcooking the breast.
  • Pan juices, roasted onion, and lemon make a simple spoonable sauce.
  • This recipe serves six without requiring a whole turkey.
  • A little hands-on preparation makes this a manageable centerpiece for Sunday dinner or a smaller holiday gathering.

Ingredients

Gather these simple ingredients for a juicy turkey breast with fragrant herbs, roasted garlic, and plenty of savory flavor.

  • Bone-in turkey breast - 1, 4 to 5 pounds, thawed
  • Unsalted butter - 3 tablespoons, softened
  • Olive oil - 1 tablespoon
  • Kosher salt - 1 teaspoon
  • Black pepper - 1/2 teaspoon
  • Dried thyme - 1 teaspoon
  • Dried rosemary - 1 teaspoon
  • Garlic cloves - 3, finely minced
  • Lemon - 1, cut into wedges
  • Yellow onion - 1 medium, quartered
  • Low-sodium chicken broth - 1 cup

How to Cook a Turkey Breast

Plan for about 20 minutes of prep, 1 hour 45 minutes of cooking, and 15 minutes of resting time. The exact roasting time can vary, so let the temperature of the turkey guide you.

Step 1: Preheat the Oven

Preheat the oven to 350°F. Giving the oven time to fully heat helps the turkey roast evenly from the start.

Step 2: Dry the Turkey

Do not rinse the raw turkey. Pat the breast dry with paper towels, discard the towels, and wash your hands and any surfaces that touched raw poultry. Dry skin browns more evenly.

Step 3: Set the Turkey in the Pan

Place the turkey breast skin-side up in a roasting pan. Keep it centered so the heat can circulate around the meat.

Step 4: Mix the Herb Butter

In a small bowl, mix the softened butter, olive oil, salt, pepper, thyme, rosemary, and garlic. Stir until the seasonings are evenly distributed through the butter.

Step 5: Rub on the Herb Butter

Gently loosen the skin without tearing it and spread a little herb butter underneath. Rub the remaining butter over the skin for an evenly seasoned, golden finish.

Step 6: Add the Onion and Lemon

Arrange the quartered onion and lemon wedges around the turkey. They will add gentle flavor to the pan juices as everything roasts.

Step 7: Pour in the Broth

Pour the chicken broth into the bottom of the pan, taking care not to pour it directly over the seasoned skin. The broth will help keep the pan juices savory and moist.

Step 8: Roast the Turkey

Roast the turkey until the thickest part reaches 165°F, about 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours. Begin checking at about 1 hour 15 minutes. Insert an instant-read thermometer into the thickest part without touching bone, and check more than one spot. Continue roasting until each spot reaches at least 165°F (74°C). If the skin browns too quickly, tent it loosely with foil.

Step 9: Baste During Roasting

If you like, spoon a little pan juice over the turkey once during the last 30 minutes of roasting. Keep the oven opening brief. Basting is optional; use the thermometer to judge doneness.

Step 10: Rest Before Slicing

Transfer the turkey to a cutting board and let it rest for 15 minutes before slicing. Resting gives the juices time to settle, so the slices stay moist.

Tips for Juicy Roasted Turkey Breast

  • Thaw the turkey completely in the refrigerator at 40°F (4°C) or below. Allow about 24 hours for a 4- to 5-pound breast, with extra time if it is still icy. Set it in a rimmed tray to catch drips.
  • Use a thermometer rather than relying only on the clock, since turkey breasts vary in size and shape.
  • Check the package before seasoning: a pre-brined or enhanced turkey breast may need less added salt.
  • Pat the skin dry before adding the herb butter for better browning.
  • Let the roasted turkey rest before slicing to help preserve its juices.
  • Slice against the grain for the most tender bites.

How to Serve Turkey Breast

  • Spoon the warm pan juices over each slice just before serving.
  • Pair the turkey with mashed potatoes, roasted carrots, or green beans.
  • Add cranberry sauce or a bright fruit relish for a sweet contrast.
  • Serve with warm rolls to catch every bit of the savory juices.
  • Use leftover turkey in sandwiches, salads, soups, or casseroles.

Make Ahead and Storage

Storing Leftovers

  • Slice leftover turkey into smaller portions and refrigerate in shallow covered containers within 2 hours of cooking, or within 1 hour if the room or outdoor temperature is above 90°F (32°C). Do not leave it on the counter until completely cool.
  • Store the turkey and pan juices together when possible to help keep the meat moist.
  • Refrigerated leftovers are best enjoyed within 3 to 4 days.

Freezing

  • Slice the cooled turkey and place it in an airtight freezer container or freezer bag.
  • Add a little pan juice or broth before sealing to protect the texture.
  • Freeze for up to 2 to 3 months and thaw overnight in the refrigerator before reheating.

Reheating

  • Place slices in a covered baking dish with a splash of broth or pan juices.
  • Warm in a 325°F oven until heated through, checking that the center reaches 165°F.
  • For a small portion, reheat gently in the microwave in short intervals, covered to retain moisture.

Bring It to the Table

This tender roasted turkey breast brings a little holiday comfort to the family table, with golden skin, fragrant herbs, and wonderful pan juices in every slice.

FAQs

Here are a few helpful answers for making this cozy turkey dinner with confidence.

How do I know when the turkey breast is done?

The turkey is done when the thickest part reaches 165°F on an instant-read thermometer. Avoid touching the bone when taking the temperature.

Can I use a boneless turkey breast?

Yes, but the cooking time may be shorter. Begin checking the temperature early and remove the turkey when the thickest part reaches 165°F.

Should I cover the turkey while it roasts?

This recipe roasts the turkey uncovered to encourage golden skin. If the skin browns too quickly, loosely tent it with foil while the turkey finishes cooking.

Why is resting the turkey important?

Resting for 15 minutes allows the juices to settle back into the meat. It also makes the turkey easier to slice neatly.
